easy.def: To have a certain look, place, or feeling.
examples: I am happy today.
The cat is on the bed.
We were at the park.

more.def: To exist, to stay in a place, or to have a certain quality.
examples: The library is next to the school.
Our teacher was late this morning because of the snow.
Whales are the largest animals on Earth.

easy.def: Sandy land next to the sea.
examples: We play on the beach.
The beach is sandy.
We built a castle on the beach.

more.def: A sandy or pebbly area beside the sea or a lake.
examples: We collected shells on the beach.
Waves washed over the sandy beach.
A lifeguard watched the beach.

easy.def: A small round piece with a hole for stringing.
examples: I made a necklace with beads.
A red bead fell on the floor.
She has a box of beads.

more.def: A small piece of glass, wood or plastic with a hole through it, used on a string to make jewelry.
examples: She strung colorful beads onto a thread to make a bracelet.
A single glass bead rolled under the couch.
The craft table had boxes of beads in every color.

easy.def: A tiny round drop of liquid.
examples: A bead of water ran down the glass.
A bead of sweat dripped.
Beads of rain hung on the leaf.

more.def: A small, round drop of liquid.
examples: Beads of water slid down the cold glass of lemonade.
A bead of sweat rolled down the runner's forehead.
Morning dew made tiny beads on the spider web.

easy.def: A line of light.
examples: A beam of sunlight came in.
The flashlight beam was bright.
The lighthouse sent a beam.

more.def: A line of light shining from something.
examples: A beam of sunlight came through the window.
The flashlight beam lit up the path.
The lighthouse sent a beam across the water.

easy.def: A long, heavy piece of wood or metal in a building.
examples: The roof has a beam.
The beam is wood.
A big beam holds up the ceiling.

more.def: A long, strong piece of wood or metal that holds up part of a building.
examples: Wooden beams held up the barn roof.
The workers lifted a steel beam into place.
The old house has beams across the ceiling.

easy.def: A seed that you can eat.
examples: I eat green beans.
Beans grow in pods.
We planted a bean.

more.def: A smooth, round or kidney-shaped seed that grows in a pod and is eaten as a vegetable.
examples: We planted a bean in a cup and watched it sprout.
Mom served green beans with dinner.
Chili is made with beans and tomatoes.

easy.def: A big strong animal with thick fur.
examples: The bear sleeps all winter.
Bears like honey.
A brown bear walked by the stream.

more.def: A large, heavy animal with thick fur and sharp claws.
examples: The bear caught a fish in the stream.
A polar bear lives in the cold north.
Black bears climb trees.

easy.def: To put up with something.
examples: I cannot bear the noise.
She bears the cold well.
He could not bear to wait.

more.def: To put up with something unpleasant.
examples: I cannot bear the loud noise.
She bore the cold without complaining.
He could not bear to see the puppy sad.

easy.def: The hair that grows on a man's chin and cheeks.
examples: Grandpa has a beard.
The man has a long beard.
He shaved his beard.

more.def: The hair that grows on a man's chin and face.
examples: Grandpa has a long white beard.
The man trimmed his beard with scissors.
The wizard in the story had a beard down to his belt.

easy.def: A big, wild animal.
examples: The beast roared in the cave.
A bear is a big beast.
The beast ran into the woods.

more.def: A large animal, especially one that is wild or strong.
examples: The hunters in the story met a huge beast in the forest.
The beast of burden carried loads up the mountain.
In the fairy tale, the beast turned out to be kind.

easy.def: To win against someone.
examples: Our team beat the red team.
I beat my dad at checkers.
She beat me in a race.

more.def: To win against someone in a game or contest.
examples: Our team beat the other school by two points.
He beat his sister at chess for the first time.
The turtle beat the hare in the old story.

easy.def: To hit again and again.
examples: Rain beat on the roof.
Beat the drum.
The waves beat on the rocks.

more.def: To hit something over and over.
examples: The drummer beat the drum in a steady rhythm.
Rain beat against the tent all night.
Beat the eggs with a whisk until they are fluffy.

easy.def: The steady pulse of music.
examples: Clap to the beat.
The song has a fast beat.
I can feel the beat of my heart.

more.def: The regular, steady pattern of sound in music, or in your heart.
examples: The dancers moved in time with the beat of the drum.
Clap along to the beat of the song.
You can feel the beat of your heart when you run.

easy.def: Very nice to look at or hear.
examples: What a beautiful flower!
The sunset is beautiful.
You made a beautiful card.

more.def: Very pleasing to see, hear, or think about.
examples: The beautiful music made everyone stop and listen.
The garden looked beautiful after the roses bloomed.
She has a beautiful singing voice.

easy.def: In a lovely way.
examples: She sang beautifully.
The garden is beautifully kept.
He drew beautifully.

more.def: In a way that is very pleasing and lovely.
examples: She sang beautifully at the concert.
The garden was beautifully kept.
The dancers moved beautifully.

easy.def: Being very nice to look at.
examples: I love the beauty of the sunset.
The beauty of the garden.
She admired the beauty of the lake.

more.def: The quality of being very pleasing to look at or hear.
examples: We admired the beauty of the mountains.
The beauty of the song made her smile.
The garden was full of beauty in spring.

easy.def: An animal with a flat tail that builds dams.
examples: The beaver built a dam.
A beaver chews wood.
The beaver has a flat tail.

more.def: A furry animal with a flat tail and strong teeth that builds dams in streams.
examples: The beaver built a dam across the stream.
A beaver chews down trees with its sharp teeth.
The beaver slapped its flat tail on the water.

easy.def: A word used to give a reason.
examples: I am happy because it is my birthday.
We stayed in because it rained.
She cried because she fell.

more.def: A word used to tell the reason for something.
examples: The ice melted because the sun was so hot.
I wore a sweater because the room was cold.
He could not play because his leg hurt.

easy.def: To wave someone closer.
examples: She beckoned me.
He beckoned to us.
The man beckoned the child.

more.def: To signal to someone to come closer by waving or nodding.
examples: She beckoned me over with her hand.
He beckoned to the waiter.
The guide beckoned us to follow her.

easy.def: To grow or change into something.
examples: A tadpole becomes a frog.
The sky became dark.
She became a nurse.

more.def: To start to be something, or to change into something different.
examples: A caterpillar will become a butterfly.
The sky became dark as the storm moved in.
He wants to become a pilot when he grows up.

easy.def: A soft place where you sleep.
examples: I go to bed at eight.
My cat sleeps on my bed.
Make your bed in the morning.

more.def: A piece of furniture with a mattress where people lie down to sleep or rest.
examples: The hotel room had two beds and a view of the sea.
I read a story every night before bed.
The nurse made the bed with clean sheets.

easy.def: A piece of ground where plants grow.
examples: We planted tulips in the flower bed.
The garden bed is full of carrots.
Weeds grew in the bed.

more.def: A small area of ground where flowers or vegetables are planted.
examples: Dad dug a new bed for the tomato plants.
Heavy rain washed the seeds out of the flower bed.
Weeds had grown in the vegetable bed all summer.

easy.def: A room where you sleep.
examples: My bedroom is upstairs.
I read in my bedroom.
The bedroom has a bed.

more.def: A room in a home where people sleep.
examples: My bedroom is at the top of the stairs.
She decorated her bedroom with posters.
The house has three bedrooms.

easy.def: The time you go to bed.
examples: Bedtime is at eight.
It is my bedtime.
We read a story at bedtime.

more.def: The time of night when you go to bed.
examples: My bedtime is at eight o'clock.
Mom reads to us at bedtime.
It is past your bedtime.

easy.def: A flying insect that makes honey.
examples: A bee buzzed by.
Bees live in a hive.
The bee stung me.

more.def: A flying insect with a striped body that collects nectar from flowers and makes honey.
examples: A bee buzzed around the flowers.
Bees live together in a hive.
The bee carried pollen on its legs.

easy.def: Meat from a cow.
examples: We had beef for dinner.
Beef is a kind of meat.
The burger is made of beef.

more.def: The meat of a cow, eaten as food.
examples: We had roast beef for dinner.
The farmers raise cattle for beef.
Dad made beef stew with carrots.

easy.def: A short, high sound.
examples: I heard a beep.
The horn gave a beep.
The microwave made a beep.

more.def: A short, high sound made by a machine or horn.
examples: The alarm clock gave a loud beep.
The microwave made a beep when the food was ready.
I heard a beep from the truck.

easy.def: To make a short, high sound.
examples: The car beeps.
The truck beeped.
The microwave beeped.

more.def: To make a short, high sound, like a horn.
examples: The truck beeped as it backed up.
The microwave beeps when the food is ready.
The driver beeped to say hello.

easy.def: Earlier than something else.
examples: Wash up before dinner.
I woke before the sun.
Brush your teeth before bed.

more.def: At an earlier time than something else, or in front of something.
examples: Please finish your homework before you play outside.
The thunder came before the rain.
He arrived at the station before noon.

easy.def: At an earlier time.
examples: I have seen it before.
She came the day before.
Have you been here before?

more.def: At some time earlier than now.
examples: I have never ridden a horse before.
We met the new teacher the day before.
Have you tried this fruit before?

easy.def: To ask for something very much.
examples: The puppy begs for a treat.
I begged Mom for a pet.
He begged to stay.

more.def: To ask for something in a strong, pleading way.
examples: The puppy begged for a bite of my sandwich.
She begged her parents to let her stay up late.
The child begged to go on the ride again.

easy.def: A person who asks for money because they are poor.
examples: The beggar sat by the road.
A beggar asked for food.
In the story, a beggar needed help.

more.def: A person who asks others for money or food because they are poor.
examples: In the story, the kind girl shared her bread with a beggar.
A beggar sat by the church steps asking for coins.
The king dressed as a beggar to learn how his people lived.

easy.def: To start.
examples: Class begins at nine.
We began to sing.
The show will begin soon.

more.def: To start doing something, or to happen for the first time.
examples: School begins at eight o'clock.
She began to paint when she was six.
The race begins when the whistle blows.

easy.def: The start of something.
examples: The beginning of the book is funny.
The beginning of the race.
At the beginning, it is easy.

more.def: The first part of something, or the time when it starts.
examples: The beginning of the movie was funny.
At the beginning of the year, we met our teacher.
Spring is the beginning of the growing season.

easy.def: A word used to say who you speak or act for.
examples: I speak on behalf of the class.
She accepted the prize on behalf of the team.
He did it on my behalf.

more.def: A word in a special phrase that means for someone or in their place.
examples: She accepted the award on behalf of the whole team.
I am writing on behalf of my class.
He said thank you on my behalf.

easy.def: To act in a good or certain way.
examples: Please behave.
The puppy behaved well.
The class behaved at the museum.

more.def: To act in a certain way, especially in a polite or proper way.
examples: The students behaved well on the bus.
Puppies sometimes do not behave when they are tired.
Please behave politely at the table.

easy.def: The way you act.
examples: Her behavior is good.
His behavior was kind.
The dog's behavior is good.

more.def: The way a person or animal acts.
examples: The class was praised for its good behavior.
Scientists study the behavior of birds.
The puppy's behavior was calm and friendly.

easy.def: At the back of something.
examples: The cat hid behind the couch.
Stand behind me in line.
The sun went behind a cloud.

more.def: At the back of something, or following after it.
examples: A rabbit hid behind the bushes in the garden.
The young ducks swam in a line behind their mother.
The sun slipped behind the mountains at the end of the day.

easy.def: Not as far along as others.
examples: The last runner fell behind.
I am behind in my reading.
Our team is behind now, but we can still win.

more.def: Farther back or less far along than others, or than planned.
examples: The hikers at the back of the group fell behind on the steep trail.
She was behind at halftime, but she scored three times and won.
I am a little behind in math because I was sick.

easy.def: To see something amazing.
examples: Behold the sunset!
We beheld a rainbow.
She beheld the castle.

more.def: To look at something, especially something wonderful.
examples: Behold the beautiful sunset!
We beheld a rainbow across the valley.
The travelers beheld a great castle.

easy.def: Something you think is true.
examples: It is my belief that she is kind.
He has a strong belief.
That is a common belief.

more.def: A strong feeling that something is true or right.
examples: It is my belief that dogs are friendly.
Their beliefs came from their family.
She has a strong belief in being kind.

easy.def: To think that something is true.
examples: I believe you.
I believe it will snow soon.
Do you believe in fairies?

more.def: To feel sure that something is true or real.
examples: She believed her team could win if they worked together.
Nobody believed him when he said he saw a bear.
I believe that practice will make me a better swimmer.

easy.def: A person who thinks something is true or good.
examples: I am a believer in kindness.
He is a believer.
She is a believer in teamwork.

more.def: A person who has faith in something, or who thinks that something is right or good.
examples: I am a believer in being kind to everyone.
She is a believer in hard work and practice.
He was once a doubter, but now he is a believer in recycling.

easy.def: A metal cup that rings when it is hit.
examples: The bell rings.
Ring the bell.
The school bell is loud.

more.def: A hollow metal object that makes a ringing sound when it is struck.
examples: The school bell rings at the end of the day.
A bell hung from the church tower.
The cat wore a tiny bell on its collar.

easy.def: To shout in a deep, loud voice.
examples: The bull bellowed.
He bellowed my name.
The giant bellowed.

more.def: To shout in a deep, loud voice, or to make a loud, deep cry like a bull.
examples: The bull bellowed in the field.
The coach bellowed across the field.
The giant bellowed in the story.

easy.def: The part of your body between your chest and your legs.
examples: My belly is full.
The baby has a round belly.
I have a belly ache.

more.def: The soft part of the body below the chest, also called the stomach or tummy.
examples: My belly was full after lunch.
The puppy rolled over to have its belly rubbed.
A bee's belly is striped.

easy.def: To be owned by someone.
examples: This book belongs to me.
The coat belongs to Sam.
Who does the toy belong to?

more.def: To be the property of a person or group, or to be owned by them.
examples: This pencil belongs to Mia.
The bike belongs to my sister.
Who does this coat belong to?

easy.def: To be in the right place.
examples: The shoes belong by the door.
Books belong on the shelf.
The spoon belongs in the drawer.

more.def: To be in the right place or group.
examples: Pencils belong in the desk, not on the floor.
A penguin belongs in cold places.
You belong on our team.

easy.def: Loved very much.
examples: My beloved pet is a dog.
The beloved teacher retired.
She hugged her beloved doll.

more.def: Very much loved by someone.
examples: The beloved teacher retired after thirty years.
She hugged her beloved teddy bear.
The beloved old dog slept by the fire.

easy.def: In a lower place.
examples: The fish swim below.
Look at the picture below.
The basement is below.

more.def: In or to a lower place than something else.
examples: We could see the village far below from the mountain top.
Some of the cave animals live far below, where it is dark.
Read the story above and answer the questions below.

easy.def: Lower than something.
examples: The cat sat below the table.
The sun went below the hills.
The temperature is below zero.

more.def: At a lower level or position than something.
examples: The submarine moved below the surface of the sea.
The temperature dropped below freezing last night.
Roots grow below the ground.

easy.def: A strip you wear around your waist.
examples: My belt holds up my pants.
He wears a belt.
The belt is brown.

more.def: A strip of leather or cloth worn around the waist.
examples: His belt had a shiny buckle.
He fastened his belt tight.
A brown leather belt held the tools.

easy.def: A loop that moves things.
examples: The belt carries bags.
The fan belt.
The belt moves boxes.

more.def: A loop of material that moves around wheels to carry or turn things.
examples: The belt carries bags at the airport.
A belt turns the wheels in the machine.
Boxes ride along the conveyor belt.

easy.def: A long seat for more than one person.
examples: We sat on the bench.
The bench is in the park.
The bench is wood.

more.def: A long seat that is often made of wood or stone, for two or more people.
examples: We sat on a bench in the park.
The players waited on the bench.
The old bench had a creaky seat.

easy.def: To make something not straight.
examples: Bend your knees.
I bend the wire.
The tree will bend in the wind.

more.def: To make something curve, or to lean your body forward.
examples: She bent down to tie her shoe.
The strong wind made the trees bend.
He bent the wire into the shape of a heart.

easy.def: A place where a road or river turns.
examples: The road has a bend.
The river makes a bend.
We turned at the bend.

more.def: A place where a road, river or path curves.
examples: The bus slowed down at the bend in the road.
A heron stood at a bend in the river.
The trail makes a sharp bend near the bridge.

easy.def: Under.
examples: The cat is beneath the table.
The fish swim beneath the boat.
I hid beneath my blanket.

more.def: Under or below something.
examples: The treasure was buried beneath an old oak tree.
Worms tunnel beneath the surface of the soil.
We sat beneath a shady tree to eat our lunch.

easy.def: Something good that helps you.
examples: Exercise has many benefits.
One benefit of reading is learning new words.
A benefit of living close is walking to school.

more.def: A good result or something that helps you.
examples: One benefit of exercise is a stronger heart.
The benefit of living near school is that you can walk.
Fresh air has many benefits for your health.

easy.def: To get something good from something.
examples: Plants benefit from rain.
We benefit from sleep.
The whole town benefited from the new park.

more.def: To be helped by something, or to be good for someone.
examples: Plants benefit from sunlight and water.
The whole town benefited from the new library.
Your muscles benefit from stretching.

easy.def: Next to.
examples: Sit beside me.
The cat is beside the dog.
The park is beside the school.

more.def: At the side of someone or something.
examples: She sat beside her friend on the bus.
The cat curled up beside the fire.
A little stream ran beside the road.

easy.def: Also.
examples: I like pizza, and besides, it is cheap.
Besides, it is late.
We have homework, and besides, it is raining.

more.def: In addition to what has been said.
examples: I do not want to go, and besides, it is late.
She is a good singer and, besides, plays the piano.
It is too cold, and besides, it is dark.

easy.def: Other than.
examples: Who is here besides us?
I like all fruit besides pears.
No one besides me knows.

more.def: Other than, or in addition to.
examples: Who else is coming besides us?
Everyone besides Sam finished the test.
No one besides the teacher knew the answer.

easy.def: Better than all the others.
examples: She is my best friend.
This is the best cake.
He is the best runner.

more.def: Better than all the rest, or of the highest quality.
examples: The best part of the trip was seeing the dolphins.
She is the best swimmer on our team.
This is the best book I have read this year.

easy.def: In the most good way.
examples: I like this best.
She sings best.
He jumps the best.

more.def: In the most successful or pleasing way.
examples: Of all the paints, I like the blue one best.
The plants grow best in warm sunshine.
She did best on the spelling test.

easy.def: To say you feel sure.
examples: I bet it will rain today.
I bet you are hungry.
I bet she finds the lost key.

more.def: To say that you strongly believe something is true.
examples: I bet the bus is late because of the snow.
My brother bet that his team would win the game.
She bet that nobody could guess the answer to her riddle.

easy.def: A promise that the one who guesses wrong gives something.
examples: I made a bet with my brother.
Dad lost the bet.
Their bet was a cookie.

more.def: An agreement that the person who guesses wrong will give something to the other person.
examples: My sister won the bet, so I had to wash the dishes.
The two friends made a bet about which team would score first.
He lost the bet and had to carry his friend's backpack.

easy.def: To break someone's trust by doing something bad to them.
examples: He would never betray a friend.
She betrayed her friend's secret.
The traitor betrayed the king.

more.def: To harm someone who trusts you, for example by telling their secret or helping their enemy.
examples: She felt hurt when her friend betrayed her secret.
In the story, the knight betrayed his king.
A good friend will not betray your trust.

easy.def: Doing something that hurts someone who trusted you.
examples: Telling his secret was a betrayal.
She felt betrayal.
The betrayal made me sad.

more.def: The act of breaking someone's trust, especially by hurting them or telling their secrets.
examples: Telling his secret to everyone felt like a betrayal.
She felt a deep sense of betrayal when her friend lied to her.
In the story, the betrayal of the king shocked the whole kingdom.

easy.def: More good than before or than another.
examples: This book is better.
I feel better now.
Her drawing is better than mine.

more.def: Of a higher quality than something else, or in improved health.
examples: Fresh bread is much better than stale bread.
I felt better after I rested for a day.
Practice will make your piano playing better.

easy.def: In a more good way.
examples: I sing better now.
She runs better than me.
Do it better next time.

more.def: In a more skillful or more pleasing way.
examples: My little sister reads better every week.
The plants grow better in the sun than in the shade.
You will do better on the test if you study.

easy.def: In the middle of two things.
examples: The cat sat between us.
The park is between two streets.
Put a pillow between the dolls.

more.def: In the space that separates two people, places or things.
examples: A small stream runs between the two hills.
My house is between the library and the bakery.
She stood between her two brothers in the photograph.

easy.def: Shared by two or more.
examples: Share the cookie between you two.
Divide the candy between the three of us.
The secret is between you and me.

more.def: Shared by, or connecting, two or more people or things.
examples: The twins split the pizza between them.
There is a strong friendship between the two dogs.
What is the difference between a frog and a toad?

easy.def: To be careful.
examples: Beware of the dog.
Beware of thin ice.
Beware of the step.

more.def: To be careful about something that may be dangerous.
examples: The sign said, "Beware of the dog."
Beware of the thin ice on the pond.
Beware of slippery steps.

easy.def: On the far side of something.
examples: The farm is beyond the hill.
Look beyond the trees.
The lake is beyond the woods.

more.def: On or to the far side of something.
examples: The farm is just beyond the hill.
A lake lies beyond the trees.
The path goes beyond the fence.
